title: Your Procrastination Profile
description: Find out the emotional reasons behind your habit of putting things off. Procrastination isn't about laziness; it's about regulating emotions.

questions.proc_1: I often put off starting a task simply because I'm afraid the result won't be perfect.
questions.proc_2: When a task looks too big, I feel paralyzed, panicked, and unsure which step to start with.
questions.proc_3: I deliberately delay tasks because the adrenaline of working right up to the deadline always makes me more productive.
questions.proc_4: When there's an important task to finish, I suddenly get absorbed in cleaning my room or tidying drawers.
questions.proc_5: I spend too much time researching and planning without ever actually executing.
questions.proc_6: Just thinking about how many steps a task takes makes me want to go to sleep.
questions.proc_7: To me, doing tasks well ahead of time feels boring, flat, and unchallenging.
questions.proc_8: I often justify answering trivial emails or tidying my inbox as 'productive work'.
questions.proc_9: If I feel I don't have enough time to finish something perfectly, I'd rather not start at all.
questions.proc_10: Seeing how long my to-do list is causes so much anxiety that I avoid looking at it altogether.
questions.proc_11: I believe I'm one of those magical people whose work is best under heavy pressure.
questions.proc_12: At the end of the day, I feel I've been busy all day, yet the most important task (Priority 1) is still untouched.
questions.proc_13: The biggest reason I procrastinate is that I care too much, or worry too much, about what people will think of my work.
questions.proc_14: I struggle to break a huge project into small, realistic daily steps I can chip away at.
questions.proc_15: I have no motivation to work at all until I realize I'm running out of time.
questions.proc_16: I keep jumping from one small task to another so my brain gets the satisfaction (dopamine) of finishing something.
questions.proc_17: Constantly editing, revising, and never being satisfied with one part over and over is my main weakness.
questions.proc_18: The fear or mental weight I imagine about a task is often far worse than actually doing it.
questions.proc_19: I really enjoy the huge sense of relief (euphoria) after successfully submitting something in the final seconds.
questions.proc_20: I often get caught up checking notifications or replying to others until I forget why I opened my laptop.
questions.proc_21: My standards and expectations for my own performance are often too high and unrealistic.
questions.proc_22: If I get stuck on the hardest part, I stop completely instead of moving to another part.
questions.proc_23: My friends or coworkers panic at my procrastination, but inside I'm always sure 'I'll get it done somehow.'
questions.proc_24: I have lots of browser tabs open at once and often switch between tasks aimlessly to avoid the core work.

results.category: The Perfectionist (Afraid to Get It Wrong)
results.description: You procrastinate out of fear of failure and the belief that everything must be perfect on the first try.
You procrastinate because the task feels enormous, leaving you frozen and unsure where to begin.
You procrastinate because, without realizing it, you enjoy the rush of working magically close to the deadline.
You procrastinate by doing a thousand small, unimportant things so you still feel productive and free of guilt.
